newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian court order puts independent TV back on air.
newsitem.headline: Serbian court order puts independent TV back on air.

text.p: The Serbian telecommunications authorities restored independent BK Television broadcasts across the country on Monday after a court ordered it to do so, BK sources said.

BK, the most trusted and popular television station in Serbia, has been blacked out across most of the country since Thursday evening as part of a battle for control of the media ahead of elections later this year.
The state telecommunications authority cut BK TV's transmission lines going south from Belgrade on Thursday, stopping its broadcasts to cities south of the capital.
"We are back on air across Serbia. I suppose it was the court order that did it," Velimir Zugic, BK's technical manager, told Reuters on Monday.
A recent poll showed BK TV was rated the most watched and most trusted station in the country by far.
Early this month RTS warned BK TV it could no longer count on the RTS transmitters to broadcast outside Belgrade, citing financial reasons.
BK TV called the move the "most flagrant attack on media freedom in Serbia and the right of citizens to be informed".
A Belgrade court on Friday ordered both the telecommunications authority and the state-run Serbian television network RTS to broadcast BK on its transmitters.
The incident followed a political upheaval in Serbia caused by election fraud last November by the ruling Socialist Party (SPS) of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.

Huge demonstrations by Serbia's Zajedno (Together) coalition of opposition groups, drawing up to 500,000 people at their peak, forced Milosevic to recognise opposition victories in the November local elections in 14 cities, including Belgrade.
The protests were the biggest-ever challenge to Milosevic's 10-year rule.

The opposition is demanding free access to the media which the SPS, fighting to revive its battered popularity ahead of presidential and parliamentary elections later this year, is reluctant to concede despite heavy pressure from the West.
